definitions.pair: a nondegenerate sign-aware cooccurring literal pair (a,b)
definitions.pair_clauses: the clauses of F containing both a and b
definitions.closed_pair: every clause containing underlying variable |a| or |b| belongs to pair_clauses and contains exactly the candidate signs a and b for those variables

theorem.name: CAP_ADMISSIBLE_CLOSED_PAIR_GUARANTEES_V3_TWO_ELIMINATION_PLAN
theorem.statement: If (a,b) is a closed pair and its apply_or_pair_v2 macro output fits the frozen N^2 cap, then the frozen v3 search has an exact plan using pivots |a| and |b| (in either suitable canonical order); both elimination intermediates stay within the macro size cap and the final live-variable count is at least one smaller than before.
proof: Because the pair is closed, after replacement no payload/untouched clause contains either underlying variable |a| or |b|. Their only remaining occurrences are in the three definitions (-e,-a), (-e,-b), (e,a,b).

Eliminate underlying variable |a|. Its two definitional parent clauses resolve to a clause containing both e and -e, hence the only cross-resolvent is tautological and is discarded exactly. The two |a|-clauses disappear and no new clause is materialized; (-e,-b) remains.
Therefore the first exact elimination strictly decreases representation size and cannot exceed the already cap-admissible macro state.
Now underlying variable |b| occurs only in the remaining binary definition (-e,-b) with one polarity, so exact elimination is pure: the clause disappears and no resolvent is generated.
The second intermediate therefore also stays below the macro state size and under the same N^2 cap.
The macro introduced only e while the two distinct old variables |a| and |b| are gone, so live-variable count decreases by at least one; in root-free mode this strictly decreases frozen progress Phi.

The v3 search enumerates every cooccurring literal pair and every ordered pair of distinct pre-macro live variables, so it will algorithmically encounter and independently replay this plan without heuristic selection.

macro_cap_bridge.statement: The closed-pair theorem composes with C025_V3_MACRO_CAP_HEADROOM_CORRIDOR: if state headroom H>=9, any closed pair is automatically macro-cap-admissible because every candidate occurs at least once; for H<9 use the exact frequency condition k_ab>=10-H.

necessary_condition_for_remaining_gap.statement: A root-free v3 availability gap cannot contain a cap-admissible closed pair. Therefore every cap-admissible candidate pair in a surviving gap witness must have external incidence of at least one underlying pair variable outside the jointly replaced pair clauses or a sign mismatch that violates closed-pair structure.

next_exact_target: Generalize from zero external incidence to bounded external incidence: derive a polynomial cap condition for macro plus first/second elimination as a function of the two pair variables' external positive/negative bucket masses.
